about.title: Artesia Slip & Fall and Premises Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Falls on someone else's property don't always look serious at first, but a torn ligament or fractured wrist can sideline you for weeks. In Artesia, these cases often happen at retail plazas along Pioneer Boulevard, businesses near South Street, or apartment properties tucked around the SR-91 corridor. California law puts the burden on you to show the property owner or manager knew, or reasonably should have known, about the hazard and didn't fix it or warn you in time. That's why what happens right after your fall matters: photos of the spill, debris, or broken step; witness names; and, when possible, a request that the business preserve any surveillance footage before it gets erased. LawProactive doesn't practice law ourselves. We're a free service that puts you in touch with an independent attorney who can evaluate your fall, explain your options under California's two-year filing deadline, and work on contingency so you owe nothing upfront.

items.title: We understand the 'notice' requirement
items.desc: California requires showing the property owner knew or should have known about the hazard. An attorney can help gather the evidence needed to establish that notice before it disappears.

items.title: We help protect your two-year window
items.desc: Premises liability claims generally must be filed within two years, and that window shrinks sharply if a government-owned property is involved. Connecting early gives an attorney time to work your case properly.

items.title: Comparative fault doesn't have to sink your claim
items.desc: California's pure comparative fault rule means you may still recover even if you were partly at fault for the fall. An independent attorney can help present your side clearly.

items.question: I fell at a store on Pioneer Boulevard. What should I do first?
items.answer: Try to photograph the hazard, the surrounding area, and your injuries before anything changes. Ask the store for an incident report and get names of any witnesses. Because surveillance footage is often overwritten within days or weeks, letting an attorney request preservation of that video quickly can matter a great deal.

items.question: Does it matter that I was partly distracted when I fell?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California follows pure comparative fault, meaning your compensation may be reduced by your percentage of fault rather than eliminated entirely. An attorney can help evaluate how that might apply to your specific fall.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after a fall in Artesia?
items.answer: Generally, California gives you two years from the date of the fall to file a premises liability lawsuit. If a government-owned property, like a public sidewalk or building, is involved, that deadline is much shorter and requires an earlier claim. Speaking with an attorney sooner rather than later helps preserve your options.
